content: I realize that I am very much dependent on leansearch to find lemmas in areas I don't know well. When it is down (just like now, for me), I am quickly stuck. Do you know if there is an alternative, or a way to make it more reliable?
I've had a lot of luck with LeanExplore

IME both LeanExplore and LeanSearch experience very long down times with no end in sight.
I haven't tried it yet but this looked pretty promising: #General announcements > Axiomatic Octo Search: Semantic Search for Any Lean Projects
(running everything locally so zero downtime)

LeanExplore has almost no down time as far as I am aware. I set it up to send me automatically messages whenever it is down, and it always turns back on almost immediately. We also recently received a grant from Renaissance Philanthropies, which will help us get dedicated compute.
We had some downtime last spring when I was running automatic updates of the index. We plan to start this back up while avoiding any of the previous pitfalls.

For Octo Search, if you have any feedback or questions they are very welcome. I had some more improvements targeted at human usage in mind that I put on the back burner, but if more people use it I can push the up my priority list.

@Snir Broshi , to be clear, locally doesn't really mean "no connection whatsover". This is still semantic search, so you need a way to go from query to embedding vector, and since we don't currently support using your own local model, it is done either by the user providing an open-router key (though it can be set only via CLI and not the UI) or axiomatic.
What you have locally is your own code, the index, and performing the search once you have the embedding for your query, plus all the infrastructure for the whole process.

(also, for the size of embedding models we are currently using, as well as I assume what @Justin Asher is using for lean-explore and what is used for lean-search, it would be impractical for a lot of people to run it on their own machine anyway).
